text.en: Meena heard her father mention paying tax. "Why do we pay tax?" she asked.

Government revenue comes from taxes and non-tax sources such as fees and dividends. Income tax is a direct tax on income. GST is an indirect tax on covered supplies, and businesses generally collect or account for it. India introduced GST in 2017, replacing many earlier indirect taxes.
A budget estimates receipts and expenditure for a financial year. The fiscal deficit compares total expenditure with receipts other than borrowing. It is distinct from an accumulated stock of debt.
Public revenue helps pay for services and facilities such as roads and schools. Governments plan and authorise spending through budget processes. Individuals and businesses must comply with applicable tax laws.
A government earns revenue and spends it on public services.

board.text: revenue

text.en: Government revenue can come from taxes and non-tax sources. Fees, interest receipts and dividends from some government enterprises are examples of non-tax revenue.

board.text: direct tax

text.en: Income tax is a direct tax on income. Goods and Services Tax is an indirect tax on covered supplies. Businesses generally account for GST and the cost can be reflected in prices.

board.text: indirect tax

text.en: Goods and Services Tax (GST) replaced many indirect taxes in 2017.

board.text: GST

text.en: A government budget presents estimated receipts and expenditure for a financial year.

board.text: budget

text.en: The fiscal deficit is the amount by which total expenditure exceeds receipts other than borrowing. It indicates the government’s borrowing requirement.

board.text: deficit

text.en: Tax money builds roads, schools, hospitals and defence, and funds welfare schemes.

board.text: revenue

text.en: People and businesses must comply with tax obligations that apply to them. Clear records and public reporting also support accountability.

board.text: direct tax

text.en: Governments fund services such as education, public health and transport. They also protect rights and provide administrative services.

board.text: Governments use resources for public purposes

text.en: Street lighting helps many people use a road at the same time. Some public services therefore need funding beyond individual bills for each use.

board.text: Public goods can benefit many people together

text.en: A school needs space and equipment, but also teachers, books and maintenance. Budgets plan for both ongoing services and longer-term assets.

board.text: Public spending includes more than buildings

text.en: A tax finances public work and is collected under legal authority. It does not usually buy one particular service for the person who pays it.

board.text: Tax is a compulsory payment under law

text.en: A licence fee can be tied to administration of that licence. Fees are one source of non-tax revenue.

board.text: A fee often relates to a particular service

text.en: Borrowed money can help meet expenditure when other receipts are insufficient. It creates an obligation to repay, so it differs from tax revenue.

board.text: Borrowing brings funds and creates debt

text.en: Income tax is charged on taxable income under the applicable law. Its liability is assessed for the person or organisation concerned.

board.text: Direct tax can be based on income

text.en: GST generally applies to covered supplies of goods or services. A business may collect or account for it as required, and customers may face a change in the final price.

board.text: An indirect tax applies to a transaction

text.en: For an indirect tax, a business can be responsible for collecting or paying the tax. The final cost may be reflected in the price paid by customers.

board.text: The legal payer and the economic burden can differ

text.en: Goods and Services Tax replaced several earlier taxes on goods and services. Some taxes and charges remain separate.

board.text: GST began in India in July 2017

text.en: The Union and states take part in the GST Council. It makes recommendations on aspects of the GST system.

board.text: The GST Council brings governments together

text.en: An itemised bill can show prices and applicable tax amounts. Actual rates and exemptions depend on rules and product categories.

board.text: A receipt can explain a purchase price

text.en: In a progressive system the average share paid in tax can rise as taxable income rises. For a school example, separate that idea from the exact rates in any year.

board.text: A progressive tax changes the share paid as income increases

text.en: A financial statement forecasts receipts and expenditure. A change in an allocation can help show which activities are being given more attention.

board.text: Budgets make priorities visible

text.en: A budget estimate is a plan. Actual tax receipts and spending can differ when prices, incomes or programme needs change.

board.text: Estimates are different from final results

text.en: Paying current operating costs is different from creating a long-lived asset. A public budget groups the two kinds of expenditure separately.

board.text: Revenue and capital spending serve different purposes

text.en: Imagine expenditure of one hundred rupees and receipts other than borrowing of eighty rupees. In the model the fiscal deficit is twenty rupees.

board.text: Fiscal deficit compares spending with non-borrowing receipts

text.en: A deficit describes a gap during one period. Debt is the total amount owed at a point in time.

board.text: A deficit and debt are not the same

text.en: Illegal non-payment or concealment can reduce government revenue and shift costs to people who comply. Tax administration includes ways to check records.

board.text: Unpaid taxes affect more than individual accounts

text.en: Changes in taxes can influence prices and spending decisions. A tax system can also distribute the cost of public services differently across households.

board.text: Tax policy can affect behaviour and distribution

text.en: Legislatures and auditors can examine whether spending followed authorisation. Public reporting helps people ask how money was used.

board.text: Public accounts support oversight

text.en: Check the period, whether the figure is planned or actual, and what is included. A number is meaningful only when you know what it measures.

problem.en: How does tax help the people?

text.en: It builds roads and schools.
It pays for hospitals and defence.
It funds welfare.

problem.en: How do a licence fee and income tax differ?

text.en: A licence fee is usually tied to a service or permission.

why.en: It is an example of non-tax revenue.

text.en: Income tax is a direct tax on taxable income under the applicable rules.

why.en: It is not a charge in exchange for a particular service.

problem.en: A model budget plans ₹100 in spending and ₹80 in receipts other than borrowing. Find the fiscal deficit.

text.en: Use total expenditure minus non-borrowing receipts.

why.en: Borrowing is excluded from the amount subtracted.
In this model the gap indicates a borrowing requirement of ₹20.

problem.en: Can someone compare a budget estimate with actual results as if they were the same?

text.en: An estimate reports what was planned.

why.en: It is made before all events in the year are known.

text.en: Actual results show recorded receipts and spending.

why.en: The labels must be kept distinct when comparing figures.

prompt.en: A friend says Income tax is an indirect tax. How will you reply?

points.en: A budget gives estimated receipts and spending for a financial year.
